objective: Deciding native networks needs a hub as well as a knot (NATIVE-HARDNESS-20261024-001), and approximate counting is settled for 28 knots and open for the six twisted Fibonacci knots (NATIVE-APPROX-20261024-001). Ask whether hub-free gadgets can imitate a hub: a three-leg function whose weight on 000 and on 111 exceeds every other value by a ratio that can be made large. An amplifiable soft hub would carry the six to bounded-degree counting, where approximation is hard unless NP = RP (Dyer, Goldberg, Jalsenius and Richerby); a uniform bound on the hub ratio would close that route. Hypothesis under test: exact hubs are impossible for every knot; windable gadgets have hub ratio at most the square root of 3 (given McQuillan) and parity and Fibonacci gadgets at most 1; the six exceed 1 but stay bounded, because diagonal pairs of configurations whose difference does not link all three terminals map onto off-diagonal pairs. Nearest known work: McQuillan, approximating Holant problems by winding (2013); Dyer, Goldberg, Jalsenius and Richerby, approximating bounded-degree counting (2010); Weitz, correlation decay (2006); Cai, Lu and Xia, Fibonacci gates. Standalone value: whether emergence without reuse can imitate reuse.
status: Complete 2026-10-25: can native emergence imitate a hub? No exact hub exists for any knot (co-independent supports). Pairs not linking all three terminals reroute onto off-diagonal values, so windable gadgets stay at most the square root of 3 (given McQuillan) and parity and no-lone gadgets at most 1; for the six open knots only linked pairs through knots empty on one side and full on the other remain. A frozen search found open-knot hub ratios only up to 65/53 with no amplification, and tree gadgets are proved to stay at most 3; gadgets with cycles remain a conjecture. Next: hubs with loops (2/3); execution deferred to the owner.
title: Can native emergence imitate a hub?
